newsitem.title: CHINA: Peugeot said pulling out of China venture.
newsitem.headline: Peugeot said pulling out of China venture.

text.p: French carmaker Peugeot SA is in the final stages of pulling out of its troubled venture in south China and the Chinese side is now looking for another foreign partner, officials and state media said on Tuesday.

"The parties concerned have agreed in principle to separate the partnership between the Chinese and French sides," the China Economic Times quoted an official as saying in the southern city of Guangzhou where the venture is based.
The newspaper gave no details of the basic accord.
A Guangzhou city government official, contacted by telephone by Reuters, said only: "The matter is being currently processed."
In Beijing, an official of the Ministry of Machine-Building Industry, said negotiations for were continuing over the terms of the withdrawal.
The Guangzhou Automobile Group, the Chinese partner in the Guangzhou Peugeot Automobile plant, will seek a new foreign partner for the venture, the newspaper said.

More than 10 foreign carmakers, including South Korea's Hyundai, Japan's Honda, and Ford Motor and General Motors of the United States, have expressed an interest in taking a stake in the venture, officials have said.
The break-up was mainly because of disagreements over the investment plan for the venture's third phase expansion project, the newspaper said.
The planned third phase would expand production capacity by 150,000 cars and would need a total investment of 4.0 billion yuan ($482 million), the newspaper said.
Guangzhou Peugeot is 30 percent owned by the French carmaker and has produced just 100,000 cars since it went into production in 1986, far below initial expectations.
Accumulated losses of the venture have reached 800 million yuan since 1994, the newspaper said.

Peugeot has been reluctant to pump more money into a venture that has been unable to reach higher production levels and turn a profit while the Chinese side has accused its French partner of trying to make too much money on the sale of parts.
French newspapers have long reported that problems with the joint venture could eventually lead to withdrawal by Peugeot.
